title: MZ How to make fixed angles like PlayStation prerendered games?

posts.author: kitsujigoku
posts.body:
I am an graphic artist and do concept art, make models, texture, etc, as I studied level design and conceptual art and decided I want my project Red Steel to have fixed angles like Final Fantasy 7, Legend of Dragoon, Parasite Eve, etc. I know the process of creating Pre-rendered sprites, angling, keying, and digitalization, etc.
What I'm trying to figure out and achieve is how do I make the ground act according to perspective, and have the player also act accordingly to the perspective line and horizon. Walks angled, gets close and further away from camera, etc.
If someone can help me do this, I'll marry you. I'm dying to get into RPG Maker but YT tutorials and even AI is not good. Ai gives old info and wrong info about 90 percent of the time and just causes more issues. I just signed up today so I can hopefully learn from the master here. Thank you all!
I am a total noob with RPG Maker MZ. I've been learning the past days with AI lol. All Youtube tutorials are just copies of one another.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Those are all 3D games, with 3D graphics rendering that can scale the 3D models as they move.
RPG Maker MZ is a 2D engine using drawn sprites. You can scale them during gameplay, but it'll be processor-intensive to be doing it constantly and there are many sizes where it will make your sprites look terrible.
MZ is not designed to emulate those kinds of games. If you really have your heart set on making a game in that style, and you're just starting anyway, you'd be better off starting with a game-making engine that's already built in 3D.
RPG Maker is meant to emulate 2D JRPGs like Final Fantasy 1-6, Dragon Quest, Phantasy Star, etc.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@kitsujigoku
You'll have to decide what is more important to you: getting the 3D graphics OR using the RPG-Maker.
There are very few and very limited plugins that activate partial 3D-Effects for the RM-Engine, and they rarely look good.
The problem is that 3D is basically intense mathematics. Most consoles have dedicated 3D processors optimized for handling those mathematics, that is how even old consoles were able to handle 3D.
The RPG-Makers have no access to such dedicated processors, even if most computers have such processors inside their display cards. That is because there are several abstraction levels between the engine and the computer's hardware.
And simulating the mathematics in the main processor is too slow to really work.
You might want to search for something called "mode 7 plugins" (I hope I remembered the term correctly), that is the best that could usually be done in the RPG-Makers.

It didn't. The camera in Super Mario RPG on SNES stays focused on the character in the center of the screen, just like the camera in RPG Maker does, and all of the sprites stay the same size regardless of where they are on the screen.
But also, as Andar says, the SNES had technology to support rudimentary 3D engines. Your computer has this technology to support 3D engines, too, but RPG Maker isn't one.

posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body:
I think you are mixing things up, even in games like Parasite Eve or Final Fantasy VII-IX in the PS1 era, only certain parts were "prerendered", the rest not really, the equivalent in RPG Maker would be tilesets.
That being said, I remember years ago, I played a demo game from a dev from Spain for RPG Maker 2003, I don't remember the name of the game and even if I did, I doubt you would be able to find it since it had a lot of copyright material in terms of music (basically ost from Naruto and Evangelion) and probably is no longer hosted.
Anyway, some of the maps in that game played with the idea of depth using the default camera in a similar maner as to how classic Doom does it. Basically you have your map made as a parallax image, and you make an "invisible" tileset where you set where the player can walk in the map. So when the character moves "away" from the camera, what you do is change the sprite to a smaller one, you do this with touch events and direction. So using Doom as an example, imagine that you don't move the player, but an enemy is far away and is walking towards you, parallax image is the stage, it's "prerendered" as you mentioned, but has "depth", as the enemy aproaches you on the y axis, every certain tiles, it "grows" in size, this is done by changing the sprite through events by placing touch events that calculate this. You just create the illusion that the sprite changes size depending on distance. In MZ probably this could be done with certain plugins, specially those who have an option to increase or decrease the size of sprites based on a percentage.
Back then it looked kind of cool that an RPG Maker 2003 game was able to have "depth" in the map, but it was just an illusion, and even then, it wasn't perfect.
The closest to a "3D" in MZ is the MV3D plugin, which I think also has a MZ port, but I'm not sure.
